title: Automated TLS Certificate Manager with ACME Protocol (DNS-01 / HTTP-01 Challenges) & Dynamic Reload
problem: Manual TLS certificate management and ad-hoc renewal scripts cause production outages when domain certificates expire unexpectedly, producing disruptive browser trust warnings and breaking critical API gateways. Furthermore, multi-tenant SaaS platforms hosting thousands of customer subdomains cannot rely on manual DNS or HTTP challenge responses without exposing DNS credentials or incurring edge server downtime during certificate reloads. This project builds a production-grade automated TLS certificate manager in Go implementing RFC 8555 ACME protocol client workflows. The daemon automatically fulfills DNS-01 and HTTP-01 validation challenges against Let's Encrypt and Pebble ACME servers, securely encrypts private keys at rest in PostgreSQL, schedules proactive renewals 30 days prior to certificate expiration, executes zero-downtime hot reloads of Nginx edge proxies, and exports certificate lifecycle metrics to Prometheus.

use_cases.title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Custom Domain TLS Automation
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise SaaS platforms hosting custom branded domains for business clients must provision trusted HTTPS endpoints automatically upon domain verification.
use_cases.second_sentence: The Go certificate manager completes automated DNS-01 challenges via cloud DNS APIs, receives signed X.509 certificates, and binds them to edge reverse proxies without human intervention.

use_cases.title: Zero-Downtime Edge Ingress Certificate Rotation
use_cases.first_sentence: E-commerce web gateways serving high volumes of active shopping carts cannot drop inflight TCP connections during monthly certificate renewals.
use_cases.second_sentence: The daemon pushes newly issued TLS bundles to Nginx via atomic configuration symlinks and sends SIGHUP signals, executing seamless zero-downtime reloads.

use_cases.title: Internal Microservice mTLS Certificate Lifecycle Management
use_cases.first_sentence: Platform engineering teams operating internal microservices need automated rotation of internal CA certificates before strict expiry windows.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system monitors certificate expiry timers in PostgreSQL, tracks remaining validity in Prometheus, and fires alerts 14 days before certificate retirement.

hard_parts: Implementing the RFC 8555 ACME state machine in Go, including account key generation, order authorization, challenge polling, and CSR finalization
Fulfilling DNS-01 challenge propagation checks and HTTP-01 ephemeral token routing through reverse proxies without exposing infrastructure DNS keys
Executing atomic certificate file updates and zero-downtime Nginx hot reloads while maintaining active persistent TLS connections
Designing proactive renewal cron workers with exponential backoff and jitter to prevent thundering herd failures against ACME rate limits
screener_signals: Clean Go codebase cleanly separating ACME protocol client logic, challenge handlers, encrypted certificate storage, and proxy reload drivers
Automated integration test report proving successful order fulfillment, DNS-01 verification, and X.509 certificate issuance against local Pebble ACME server
Anti-fake verification script presenting an expired certificate or invalid ACME signature and confirming immediate handshake failure and validation rejection

architecture.data_flow: The renewal scheduler identifies domains with certificates expiring within 30 days from PostgreSQL; the ACME client initiates an order request with the ACME server; the server returns challenge URLs; the challenge engine creates an ephemeral HTTP-01 token endpoint or publishes a DNS-01 TXT record; the ACME server validates the challenge and issues authorization; the Go client generates an ECDSA keypair, signs a Certificate Signing Request (CSR), and finalizes the order; the signed X.509 certificate chain is downloaded, encrypted, and saved to PostgreSQL; the reload controller atomically swaps the certificate file on disk and signals Nginx; Nginx hot-reloads TLS contexts without dropping in-flight requests; Prometheus scrapes remaining validity metrics.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Cryptographic ECDSA/RSA key signing and ACME SHA-256 token authorizations validated by RFC 8555 conformance checks.

targets.target: 10 of 10 expiring certificates scheduled and 40 of 40 non-expiring certificates ignored

riskiest_component.name: Outages from Defective Certificate Symlink Swapping or Failed Nginx Reloads
riskiest_component.mitigation: Validate newly issued certificates via OpenSSL verify against local CA bundle before writing symlink and sending SIGHUP.
